back_blocks.md: A **scalar** is a quantity that has **magnitude** but **no direction** (e.g. mass).

cards.back_md: A **scalar** is a quantity that has **magnitude** but **no direction** (e.g. mass).

back_blocks.md: A **vector** is a quantity that has both **magnitude** and **direction** (e.g. weight).

cards.back_md: A **vector** is a quantity that has both **magnitude** and **direction** (e.g. weight).

front_blocks.md: Give three examples each of scalar and vector quantities.

back_blocks.md:
- **Scalars**: distance, speed, mass (also time, energy, volume, density, pressure, charge, temperature)
- **Vectors**: displacement, velocity, acceleration (also force, momentum)

front_blocks.md: Describe the triangle method for adding two vectors.

back_blocks.md: Link the vectors **head-to-tail**. The **resultant** vector connects the **tail of the first** vector to the **head of the second**.

cards.front_md: Describe the triangle method for adding two vectors.
cards.back_md: Link the vectors **head-to-tail**. The **resultant** vector connects the **tail of the first** vector to the **head of the second**.

front_blocks.md: Describe the parallelogram method for adding two vectors.

back_blocks.md: Link the vectors **tail-to-tail** and complete the **parallelogram**. The **resultant** is the **diagonal** of the parallelogram.

cards.front_md: Describe the parallelogram method for adding two vectors.
cards.back_md: Link the vectors **tail-to-tail** and complete the **parallelogram**. The **resultant** is the **diagonal** of the parallelogram.

front_blocks.md: A vector *F* acts at angle *θ* to the horizontal. What are its horizontal and vertical components?

back_blocks.md:
- Horizontal: $F_{x} = F \mathrm{cos} θ$
- Vertical: $F_{y} = F \mathrm{sin} θ$

back_blocks.md: Three coplanar forces acting on an object in equilibrium form a **closed** vector triangle.

front_blocks.md: An object moving at constant speed must also have constant velocity.

back_blocks.md: If the object **changes direction**, its **velocity changes** even though its speed stays constant, because velocity is a **vector**.

cards.front_md:
**True or False?**

An object moving at constant speed must also have constant velocity.
cards.back_md:
**False.**

If the object **changes direction**, its **velocity changes** even though its speed stays constant, because velocity is a **vector**.
